english.title: Cause death by driving without due care / consideration while unfit through drugs
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused the death of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DECEASED AND DATE OF DEATH IF DIFFERENT FROM DATE OF DRIVING..) by driving a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a

(A)_[road,]_
(B)_[public place,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), without

(C)_[due care and attention,]_
(D)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the road,]_
(E)_[reasonable consideration for other persons using the place,]_

and at a time when you were unfit to drive through drugs.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3A(1)(a) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from the 28th June 2022 due to changes made by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022, which increased the penalty on indictment from 14 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. For the offence applying before the 28th June 2022, see H10173.
(ii) The minimum period of obligatory disqualification for this offence under section 34 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 was increased by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. See section 34(3), 34(3A) and 34(4ZA) which in some cases, increases the disqualification period to ten or five years.
(iii) For the purposes of section 3A, a person is taken to be unfit to drive at any time when his/her ability to drive properly is impaired.
(iv) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for alternative verdicts.
(v) Officers should ensure that they know the C.P.S. guidelines for this offence before preparing any charges.

other.penalty:
